:::{#thm-deriv-const}
#### Constant rule

If $c$ is [constant with respect to](vector-calculus.qmd#def-constant-wrt-vector) $x$, then

$$\deriv{x}c = 0$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/videos/_note-video-deriv-const.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-deriv-const-factor}
#### Constant multiple rule

If $a$ is [constant with respect to](vector-calculus.qmd#def-constant-wrt-vector) $x$
and $y$ is a [differentiable function](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) of $x$, then:
$$\deriv{x}ay = a \derivf{y}{x}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/videos/_note-video-deriv-const-factor.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-deriv-polynomial}
#### Power rule

For every [real number](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $q$ and every $x > 0$
[@wikipedia_power_rule],
the [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of the [power](algebra.qmd#def-real-power) $x^q$ is:

$$\deriv{x}x^q = qx^{q-1}$$

When $q$ is a [positive integer](number-systems.qmd#def-positive-integer),
the same [formula](expressions-algorithms.qmd#def-closed-form-expression) holds for every [real](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $x$.

:::

{{< include mds/_subfiles/videos/_note-video-power-rule.qmd >}}

:::{#thm-deriv-log}

#### Derivative of natural logarithm

For every $x > 0$,
the [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of the [natural logarithm](algebra.qmd#def-natural-log) is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dlogf{x}
&= \frac{1}{x} \\
&= x^{-1}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/calculus-review/_exr-miller-deriv-log-simplify.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-deriv-exp}
#### Derivative of exponential

For every [real](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $x$,
the [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of the [exponential function](algebra.qmd#def-exponential-function) is:

$$\dexpf{x} = \expf{x}$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-deriv-sin}
#### Derivative of sine

For every [real](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $x$,
the [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of the [sine](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-sine) [function](functions.qmd#def-function) is:

$$\deriv{x}\sin x = \cos x$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-deriv-cos}
#### Derivative of cosine

For every [real](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $x$,
the [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) of the [cosine](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-cosine-sine) [function](functions.qmd#def-function) is:

$$\deriv{x}\cos x = -\sin x$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-product-rule}
#### Product rule

If $a$ and $b$ are [differentiable functions](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) of $x$
[@wikipedia_product_rule], then

$$(ab)' = ab' + ba'$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/videos/_note-video-product-rule.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/calculus-review/_exr-miller-deriv-product-poly-cos.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/calculus-review/_exr-miller-deriv-second-product.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-quotient-rule}
#### Quotient rule

If $a$ and $b$ are [differentiable functions](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) of $x$
[@wikipedia_quotient_rule]
and $b \neq 0$, then

$$(a/b)' = a'/b - (a/b^2)b'$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/videos/_note-video-quotient-rule.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include mds/_subfiles/calculus-review/_exr-miller-deriv-quotient-or-factor.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-chain-rule}
#### Chain rule

If $a$ is a [differentiable function](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) of $b$
[@wikipedia_chain_rule],
and $b$ is a differentiable function of $c$,
then $a$ is a differentiable function of $c$, and

$$\ba
\dif{a}{c} &=
\dif{a}{b} \dif{b}{c}
\\
&= \dif{b}{c} \dif{a}{b}
\ea
$$

or in Lagrange's notation (@def-derivative),
if $g$ is [differentiable at](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) $x$
and $f$ is differentiable at $g(x)$,
then for the [composition](functions.qmd#def-composition) $f \circ g$,
with [inner function](functions.qmd#def-inner-function) $g$ and [outer function](functions.qmd#def-outer-function) $f$:

$$(f(g(x)))' = g'(x) f'(g(x))$$
:::

:::{#cor-deriv-log-chain}

#### Chain rule for logarithms

If $f$ is [differentiable at](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) $x$ and $f(x) > 0$, then

$$
\dif{}{x}\logf{f(x)} = \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}
$$

:::

::: proof
Apply @thm-chain-rule and @thm-deriv-log:

$$
\ba
\dif{}{x}\logf{f(x)}
&= f'(x) \cd \dlogf{f(x)}
&& \text{(chain rule, with } g = f \text{ and outer function } \log \text{)}
\\
&= f'(x) \cd \frac{1}{f(x)}
&& \text{(derivative of } \log \text{, valid because } f(x) > 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$
:::
